rationale: Direct cohort analysis across the available literature confirms that individuals carrying heterozygous de novo missense variants in MAPK8IP3 present with a significantly higher burden and penetrance of major structural central nervous system malformations—including corpus callosum hypoplasia, cerebral/cerebellar atrophy, and perisylvian polymicrogyria—as well as more severe clinical and cognitive impairment compared to individuals with predicted loss-of-function (LOF) or truncating variants. Multiple independent cohorts, including the systematic series of 32 individuals in Sudnawa et al. (2026) and 13 individuals in Platzer et al. (2019), demonstrate that major structural anomalies cluster consistently in recurrent missense variants (likely mediated by dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanisms affecting axonal transport), whereas truncating variants exhibit incomplete penetrance or a milder, highly variable neurodevelopmental spectrum.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 32 individuals with heterozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic MAPK8IP3 variants (62.5% missense, 34.4% predicted LOF), missense variants were significantly associated with more severe clinical symptoms than loss-of-function variants. Thinning of the corpus callosum was documented in 62.1% of patients overall.

evidence.text: Brain anomalies including perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants in MAPK8IP3, within a cohort of 13 unrelated individuals harboring six missense and three truncating variants.

evidence.text: Five individuals from four families with recurrent de novo missense variants c.1732C>T (p.Arg578Cys) and c.3436C>T (p.Arg1146Cys) presented with a consistent core phenotype including intellectual disability, spastic diplegia, cerebral atrophy, and corpus callosum hypoplasia.

source.title: Recurrent de novo MAPK8IP3 variants cause neurological phenotypes
source.quote: The core phenotype includes spastic diplegia, intellectual disability, cerebral atrophy, and corpus callosum hypoplasia.

evidence.text: Characterization of an inherited truncating splice-site variant (c.2630-2_2630-1del, p.Gly877Valfs*36) across three family members demonstrated marked interindividual phenotypic variability, ranging from mild specific learning difficulties without major dysgenesis to severe developmental delay, confirming that truncating alleles exhibit variable expressivity and do not uniformly produce the severe brain malformations seen in recurrent missense cohorts.

source.title: Characterization of a novel inherited splice-site variant in MAPK8IP3 expands the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders
source.quote: Notably, despite carrying an identical genotype, the three affected individuals exhibited marked interindividual variability in clinical severity, ranging from mild specific learning difficulties to global developmental delay with severe intellectual disability and autism.

new_directions.question_text: Does dominant-negative inhibition of retrograde axonal cargo transport by mutant JIP3 missense proteins account for the marked difference in cortical and callosal morphogenesis compared to simple haploinsufficiency?
new_directions.rationale: Comparing isogenic human cerebral organoids harboring recurrent de novo missense alleles (e.g., p.Arg578Cys) against heterozygous and homozygous truncating knockout alleles will elucidate whether dominant-negative interference with dynein/kinesin trafficking drives severe structural brain malformations.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of patients harboring heterozygous truncating or LOF variants in MAPK8IP3 present with completely normal brain MRI findings compared to missense variants in international multicenter cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic blinded re-review of neuroimaging across all reported LOF versus missense carriers will provide precise diagnostic odds ratios and quantitative penetrance values for corpus callosum hypoplasia and cerebellar atrophy.
